```{python}
#| output: false
import glob
import json
import sys
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import xgboost as xgb
from pathlib import Path
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_line, geom_col, geom_abline, geom_jitter,
    geom_errorbar, geom_hline, facet_wrap,
    labs, theme_minimal, coord_flip, scale_color_manual,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, display

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "nhl" / "pbp" / "parquet").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "python"))
from nhl_data_build import xg_train as xt

files = sorted(glob.glob(str(ROOT / "nhl" / "pbp" / "parquet" / "play_by_play_*.parquet")))
pbp = pl.concat([pl.read_parquet(f) for f in files], how="diagonal_relaxed")
boosters = {}
for v in ("5v5", "st"):
    b = xgb.Booster()
    b.load_model(str(ROOT / "models" / f"xg_model_{v}.json"))
    boosters[v] = b

# The two sidecars the python trainer writes beside the boosters. They are committed with the
# first python retrain that passes the frozen gates; until then META/SPLIT are None and the
# evaluation replays the trainer's seed-37 game-grouped split (a NEAR-holdout) and says so.
_meta_path = ROOT / "models" / "xg_model_meta.json"
META = json.loads(_meta_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if _meta_path.is_file() else None
SPLIT = json.loads((ROOT / "models" / META["split_file"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if META else None
if META and not all(f"info_{v}" in META and v in (SPLIT or {}) for v in ("5v5", "st")):
    META = SPLIT = None  # a half-populated sidecar (one variant retrained) is not a fit to quote
from nhl_model_02_xg_st import _ST_DRIFT_MAX_ABS_Z, st_gates
# Frozen gates as observed at the 2026-04 R fit (the README table); the meta supersedes them when committed.
FROZEN = {"5v5": {"cv_auc": 0.8322, "cv_logloss": 0.2053, "floor": 0.82},
          "st": {"cv_auc": 0.8213, "cv_logloss": 0.2567, "floor": 0.81}}

def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))
```

The fastRhockey xG suite estimates the probability that an unblocked shot
becomes a goal, in two strength regimes: **5v5** (all non-shootout,
non-penalty-shot unblocked shots) and **special teams** (power play /
short-handed). A third component, the **penalty-shot constant**, is the
historical conversion rate computed at train time. The suite's output ships
as the xG columns inside every published `nhl_pbp_full` season asset — the
model never ships alone; it reaches consumers embedded in the play-by-play.

The models are XGBoost binary classifiers (logloss objective), a faithful
reproduction lineage of the hockeyR xG recipe (Morse 2022), re-fit on this
repository's own committed corpus by `python/nhl_data_build/xg_train.py`
(canonical R twin `R/build_xg_model.R`). The fitted boosters are **committed
in this repo** (`models/xg_model_{5v5,st}.json`) — that is the promotion step
— and every figure and number below is computed at render time from those
committed artifacts plus the committed play-by-play. The python trainer also
writes two sidecars beside the boosters, `xg_model_meta.json` (feature lists,
training-time CV and holdout metrics, per-season calibration) and
`xg_model_split.json` (the train/test `game_id` partition); when they are
committed the evaluation below scores the *exact* held-out games, otherwise it
replays the trainer's split recipe on today's corpus and labels the result a
near-holdout.

## Training data

```{python}
seasons_tbl = (
    pbp.filter(pl.col("event_type").is_in(xt._FENWICK))
    .group_by("season").agg(
        pl.col("game_id").n_unique().alias("games"),
        pl.len().alias("fenwick_events"),
        (pl.col("event_type") == "GOAL").mean().alias("goal_share"),
    ).sort("season")
)
gt_show(
    GT(seasons_tbl.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Committed NHL play-by-play corpus, by season",
                subtitle="unblocked shot events (SHOT / MISSED_SHOT / GOAL); computed at render time")
    .fmt_number(columns=["fenwick_events"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_percent(columns="goal_share", decimals=1)
)
```

Training corpus: this repository's committed play-by-play
(`nhl/pbp/parquet/`, seasons listed above, ~13.6M events). Seasons are
grouped into **five era buckets** (2011–2013, 2014–2018, 2019–2021,
2022–2024, 2025-on) that enter as one-hot features, so rule- and
tracking-era shifts are modeled rather than silently biasing the fit. The
5v5/ST split is a modeling decision, not a convenience: shooting talent and
shot-quality distributions differ enough across strength states that a single
pooled model miscalibrates the power play.

## Exploratory data analysis

```{python}
#| output: false
frames, holdout, oot = {}, {}, {}
rng = np.random.default_rng(xt._SEED)
for v in ("5v5", "st"):
    fr = xt.prepare_training_frame(pbp, variant=v)
    frames[v] = fr
    if SPLIT:
        test_ids = SPLIT[v]["test_game_ids"]
        seen_ids = test_ids + SPLIT[v]["train_game_ids"]
        holdout[v] = fr.filter(pl.col("game_id").is_in(test_ids))
        oot[v] = fr.filter(pl.col("game_id").is_in(seen_ids).not_())  # games that landed after the fit
    else:  # replay the trainer's seed-37 game-grouped 80/20 recipe on today's corpus: a NEAR-holdout
        tr, te = xt._grouped_split(fr, rng)
        _ = rng.permutation(tr["game_id"].unique().to_list())  # replay the fold draw
        holdout[v], oot[v] = te, fr.head(0)
EVAL_LABEL = "exact holdout" if SPLIT else "near-holdout (seed-37 replay)"
f5 = frames["5v5"]
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Goal rate by shot distance, 5v5 model frame — the dominant feature."
d = (
    f5.with_columns((pl.col("shot_distance") / 5).floor().alias("bin"))
    .group_by("bin").agg(pl.col("goal").mean().alias("goal_rate"),
                          pl.len().alias("n"), pl.col("shot_distance").mean().alias("dist"))
    .filter((pl.col("n") >= 500) & (pl.col("dist") <= 90)).sort("dist")
)
(
    ggplot(d.to_pandas(), aes("dist", "goal_rate"))
    + geom_point(aes(size="n"), color="#2a6f97", alpha=0.8) + geom_line(color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="shot distance (ft)", y="observed goal rate",
           title="NHL goal rate by shot distance (5v5 frame)")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
shot_mix = (
    f5.select([c for c in xt._SHOT_TYPE_COL.values() if c in f5.columns] + ["goal"])
    .unpivot(index="goal", variable_name="shot_type", value_name="is_type")
    .filter(pl.col("is_type") == 1)
    .group_by("shot_type").agg(pl.len().alias("shots"), pl.col("goal").mean().alias("goal_rate"))
    .sort("shots", descending=True)
)
gt_show(
    GT(shot_mix.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Shot-type mix and conversion (5v5 frame)")
    .fmt_number(columns="shots", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_percent(columns="goal_rate", decimals=1)
)
```

Distance dominates conversion — from ~25% at the crease to ~2% beyond 60 ft —
and the shot-type table explains the one-hot block: tips and deflections
convert well above wrist shots from similar range, and the model needs the
type to separate them. The special-teams frame adds `total_skaters_on` and
`event_team_advantage`, the two features that encode the man-advantage state.

## SHAP

TreeSHAP attributions come directly from the committed boosters
(`pred_contribs=True` — exact for tree ensembles, no extra dependency). The
distribution of per-shot attributions for the top features shows how each
one moves individual shots on the log-odds scale:

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "TreeSHAP per-shot attributions, 5v5 booster, top 8 features by mean |SHAP|; 4,000-shot sample."
b5 = boosters["5v5"]
feats5 = b5.feature_names
rs = np.random.default_rng(11)
samp_idx = rs.choice(f5.height, size=min(4000, f5.height), replace=False)
Xs = f5.select(feats5).to_numpy().astype(float)[samp_idx]
contribs = b5.predict(xgb.DMatrix(Xs, feature_names=feats5), pred_contribs=True)[:, :-1]
mean_abs = np.abs(contribs).mean(axis=0)
order = np.argsort(mean_abs)[::-1][:8]
rows = []
for j in order:
    for i in range(Xs.shape[0]):
        rows.append({"feature": feats5[j], "shap": float(contribs[i, j])})
shap_df = pl.DataFrame(rows).to_pandas()
(
    ggplot(shap_df, aes("feature", "shap"))
    + geom_jitter(width=0.25, alpha=0.05, size=0.4, color="#2a6f97")
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(x="", y="SHAP (log-odds)", title="TreeSHAP attributions per shot — 5v5")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
shap_tbl = pl.DataFrame({
    "feature": [feats5[j] for j in order],
    "mean_abs_shap": [float(mean_abs[j]) for j in order],
})
gt_show(
    GT(shap_tbl.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Mean |SHAP| — 5v5 booster, 4,000-shot sample")
    .fmt_number(columns="mean_abs_shap", decimals=4)
)
```

## Evaluation

Two views, honestly labeled. First, the **training-time metrics**: grouped
5-fold CV on the 80% side (the gated number) and the game-grouped 20% holdout
the fit never saw. They come from `models/xg_model_meta.json` when a python
sidecar is committed, otherwise from the 2026-04 R fit's console output as
frozen in the README (CV only — that run persisted no holdout metrics and no
partition, which is exactly what the sidecars fix). The gate floors are frozen
just below the 2026-04 values (5v5 cv AUC ≥ 0.82, ST ≥ 0.81) and are never
lowered; a real retrain below them fails (`--quick` smoke runs tolerate misses).

```{python}
#| output: asis
if META:
    print("**Sidecar state:** `xg_model_meta.json` + `xg_model_split.json` are committed — the holdout below is the exact "
          f"training-time partition (fit {max(META[f'info_{v}']['trained_at'] for v in ('5v5', 'st'))[:10]}).")
else:
    print("**Sidecar state:** no python sidecar is committed yet — the committed boosters are the 2026-04 R fit. The python "
          "trainer writes both sidecars on every run, but its 2026-09-02 retrain on this repository's parquet frame fell "
          "below the frozen floors (special teams cv AUC **0.7569** vs ≥ 0.81) and was not promoted (`models/ledger.jsonl`). "
          "Gates are never lowered, so the sidecars land with the first passing retrain; until then the evaluation below "
          "replays the trainer's seed-37 game-grouped split on today's corpus and is a *near*-holdout — some evaluation "
          "games were in the boosters' training data.")
```

```{python}
rows = []
for v in ("5v5", "st"):

    if META:

            "CV AUC": i["cv_auc"], "CV log-loss": i["cv_logloss"],
            "holdout AUC": i["test_auc"], "holdout log-loss": i["test_logloss"],
            "baseline log-loss": i.get("baseline_logloss"),

        })
    else:
        rows.append({
            "variant": v, "source": "2026-04 R fit (README; CV only)",
            "train shots": None, "holdout shots": None, "holdout games": None,
            "CV AUC": fz["cv_auc"], "CV log-loss": fz["cv_logloss"],
            "holdout AUC": None, "holdout log-loss": None, "baseline log-loss": None,

        })
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame(rows).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Training-time metrics",
                subtitle="grouped 5-fold CV on the 80% side; game-grouped 20% holdout; floors frozen, never lowered")
    .fmt_number(columns=["train shots", "holdout shots", "holdout games"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns=["CV AUC", "CV log-loss", "holdout AUC", "holdout log-loss", "baseline log-loss"], decimals=4)
    .sub_missing(missing_text="—")

```

Second, the **held-out games re-scored at render time** by the committed
boosters. With a committed split file this is today's corpus filtered to the
persisted `test_game_ids`; games that landed after the fit are in neither list
and are reported separately as **out-of-time** shots — an honest forward test
that grows as seasons land — and `Δ vs meta` (render-time holdout AUC minus
the meta's) is exactly 0 unless the committed play-by-play was repaired after
the fit. Without a split file the set is the seed-37 replay described above.

```{python}
def eval_rows(label, frames_by_v):
    out = []
    for v in ("5v5", "st"):
        te, b, i = frames_by_v[v], boosters[v], (META[f"info_{v}"] if META else None)
        row = {"variant": v, "set": label, "shots": te.height, "games": te["game_id"].n_unique()}
        if te.height:
            X = te.select(b.feature_names).to_numpy().astype(float)
            y = te["goal"].to_numpy().astype(float)
            p = b.predict(xgb.DMatrix(X, feature_names=b.feature_names))
            auc = xt._rank_auc(p, y)
            base = i["goal_rate"] if i else float(frames[v]["goal"].mean())
            row |= {"goal_rate": float(y.mean()), "logloss": xt._logloss(y, p),
                    "baseline_logloss": xt._logloss(y, np.full_like(p, base)),
                    "rank_AUC": auc,
                    "Δ vs meta": (auc - i["test_auc"]) if (i and label == EVAL_LABEL and i.get("test_auc") is not None) else None}
        out.append(row)
    return out
ev = pl.DataFrame(eval_rows(EVAL_LABEL, holdout) + eval_rows("out-of-time (post-fit games)", oot))
n_oot = int(ev.filter(pl.col("set").str.starts_with("out-of-time"))["games"].sum())
gt_show(
    GT(ev.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Held-out evaluation — {EVAL_LABEL} (render-time, current corpus)",
                subtitle=("test_game_ids from models/xg_model_split.json" if SPLIT else "seed-37 game-grouped 80/20 replay; committed boosters scored on the 20% side")
                         + f"; {n_oot} post-fit games in the out-of-time set")
    .fmt_number(columns=["shots", "games"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_percent(columns="goal_rate", decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns=["logloss", "baseline_logloss", "rank_AUC", "Δ vs meta"], decimals=4)
    .sub_missing(missing_text="—")
)
```

## Per-season calibration drift

The special-teams sample is ~5× smaller than 5v5, so its AUC floor alone
cannot see a season whose *level* drifts — a rule or tracking change that
shifts conversion without reordering shots. The monitor is the binomial
calibration z-score per season, `z = (goals − ΣxG) / sqrt(ΣxG · (1 − xG))`: a
season the model prices correctly has |z| ~ N(0, 1) whatever its shot count,
which is what makes `max |z|` comparable across seasons of unequal size. The
trainer records this table in `info_st.per_season_calibration` at every
retrain (`xg_train.per_season_calibration`), and stage `nhl_model_02_xg_st`
gates on `max |z| ≤ _ST_DRIFT_MAX_ABS_Z` — a ceiling derived from the value
observed on the exact holdout of the trusted retrain and never raised (see
`models/REGISTRY.md`). The same statistic is recomputed here at render time on
the held-out shots, with post-fit seasons appended as out-of-time rows.

```{python}
def season_rows(v, frames_by_v, label):
    te = frames_by_v[v]
    if te.height == 0:
        return []
    b = boosters[v]
    p = b.predict(xgb.DMatrix(te.select(b.feature_names).to_numpy().astype(float), feature_names=b.feature_names))
    return [{"variant": v, "set": label, **r}
            for r in xt.per_season_calibration(te["game_id"].to_numpy(), te["goal"].to_numpy().astype(float), p)]
cal = pl.DataFrame(
    season_rows("st", holdout, "holdout") + season_rows("st", oot, "out-of-time")
    + season_rows("5v5", holdout, "holdout") + season_rows("5v5", oot, "out-of-time")
)
st_tbl = cal.filter(pl.col("variant") == "st").select("set", "season", "n", "goals", "xg_sum", "ratio", "z", "auc")
st_max_z = float(cal.filter((pl.col("variant") == "st") & (pl.col("set") != "out-of-time"))["z"].abs().max())
gt_show(
    GT(st_tbl.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Special-teams calibration by season — {EVAL_LABEL} (+ out-of-time)",
                subtitle="ratio = goals / ΣxG; z = binomial calibration z-score; auc = per-season rank AUC")
    .fmt_number(columns=["n", "goals"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns=["xg_sum"], decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns=["ratio", "auc"], decimals=3)
    .fmt_number(columns=["z"], decimals=2)
)
```

```{python}
if META:
    verdict, src = st_gates(META["info_st"]), "committed xg_model_meta.json"
else:  # no python meta: evaluate the drift statistic on the render-time held-out ST shots
    verdict, src = st_gates({"cv_auc": None, "max_abs_season_z": round(st_max_z, 3)}), f"render-time {EVAL_LABEL}"
gate_tbl = pl.DataFrame({
    "check": ["cv AUC ≥ 0.81", "ST drift: max |z| over held-out seasons ≤ ceiling", "stage verdict"],
    "observed": [str(verdict["cv_auc"]) if verdict["cv_auc"] is not None else "n/a (no python meta)",
                 str(verdict["st_max_abs_season_z"]), ""],
    "threshold": ["0.81", str(verdict["st_drift_ceiling"]), ""],
    "pass": [str(verdict["cv_auc"] >= 0.81) if verdict["cv_auc"] is not None else "n/a",
             str(verdict["st_drift_pass"]), str(verdict["gate_pass"]) if META else "n/a"],
})
gt_show(GT(gate_tbl.to_pandas()).tab_header(title="Stage gates (nhl_model_02_xg_st.st_gates)", subtitle=f"evaluated on the {src}"))
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Per-season calibration: observed goals / ΣxG (points) against the ±2 SE band a calibrated model occupies (bars); the second point shape marks out-of-time seasons."
cd = cal.with_columns(pl.col("season").cast(pl.Utf8)).to_pandas()
(
    ggplot(cd, aes("season", "ratio", color="variant"))
    + geom_hline(yintercept=1, linetype="dashed", color="gray")
    + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin="1 - 2 * se_ratio", ymax="1 + 2 * se_ratio"), width=0.4, alpha=0.5)
    + geom_point(aes(shape="set"), size=2.5)
    + facet_wrap("~variant", ncol=1)
    + labs(x="season (start year)", y="goals / ΣxG", title=f"Per-season calibration — {EVAL_LABEL}")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if META:
    print("Both boosters carry era one-hots, so a booster fit on this frame sits inside the band in every season it was "
          "trained on; the informative rows are the out-of-time ones, which is where a level drift first shows.")
else:
    print(f"A booster calibrated to this frame sits inside the band in every season it was trained on — the 2026-09-02 "
          f"python special-teams retrain did (max |z| 2.008 on its exact holdout, the observation that set the {_ST_DRIFT_MAX_ABS_Z} "
          f"ceiling). The committed 2026-04 R boosters do **not** on this frame (max |z| {st_max_z:.1f} here): they score "
          "25–30% too high on every season through 2023-24 and only 2024-25 / 2025-26 come close — a level miscalibration, "
          "not drift, recorded under *Known issue* below. The drift ceiling has teeth: it fails exactly this.")
```


## Results — players and teams

```{python}
latest = int(pbp["season"].cast(pl.Int64).max())
cur = pbp.filter(pl.col("season").cast(pl.Int64) == latest)
fr_cur = xt.prepare_training_frame(cur, variant="5v5")
shooter = (
    xt._harmonize(cur).with_columns(secondary_type=xt._norm_secondary())
)
# score the current season's 5v5 frame with the committed booster
pcur = boosters["5v5"].predict(
    xgb.DMatrix(fr_cur.select(feats5).to_numpy().astype(float), feature_names=feats5))
# re-attach shooter identity by rebuilding the same filter chain (incl. the
# null-drop set: every nullable feature in prepare_training_frame's keep list
# derives from shot_distance / shot_angle / time_since_last / last_x / last_y)
def frame_with_identity(pbp_in):
    df = xt._harmonize(pbp_in).with_columns(secondary_type=xt._norm_secondary())
    df = df.filter(
        (pl.col("period_type") != "SHOOTOUT")
        & ((pl.col("secondary_type") != "Penalty Shot") | pl.col("secondary_type").is_null())
    )
    grp = "game_id"
    df = df.with_columns(
        last_event_type=pl.col("event_type").shift(1).over(grp),
        time_since_last=pl.col("game_seconds") - pl.col("game_seconds").shift(1).over(grp),
        last_x=pl.col("x").shift(1).over(grp),
        last_y=pl.col("y").shift(1).over(grp),
    )
    df = df.filter(pl.col("event_type").is_in(xt._FENWICK)
                   & pl.col("last_event_type").is_in(xt._VALID_LAST))
    return df.drop_nulls(subset=["shot_distance", "shot_angle", "time_since_last",
                                 "last_x", "last_y"])
ident = frame_with_identity(cur).select(
    "event_player_1_name", "event_player_1_id", "event_team", "event_type")
assert ident.height == fr_cur.height  # same filter chain, row-aligned
scored = ident.with_columns(pl.Series("xg", pcur))
players = (
    scored.group_by("event_player_1_id")
    .agg(pl.col("event_player_1_name").first().alias("player"),
         pl.col("event_team").last().alias("team"),
         pl.len().alias("shots"),
         pl.col("xg").sum().alias("xG"),
         (pl.col("event_type") == "GOAL").sum().alias("goals"))
    .drop_nulls("event_player_1_id")
    .with_columns((pl.col("goals") - pl.col("xG")).alias("GAX"))
    .sort("xG", descending=True).head(15)
    .with_columns(
        ("<img src='https://assets.nhle.com/mugs/nhl/latest/"
         + pl.col("event_player_1_id").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8)
         + ".png' height='42'/>").alias("headshot"))
)
gt_show(
    GT(players.select("headshot", "player", "team", "shots", "xG", "goals", "GAX").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Top 15 skaters by 5v5 expected goals — season {str(latest)[:4]}-{str(latest)[4:]}",
                subtitle="unblocked 5v5 shots scored by the committed booster; GAX = goals above expected")
    .fmt_markdown(columns="headshot")
    .fmt_number(columns=["xG", "GAX"], decimals=2)
    .cols_label(headshot="", player="Player", team="Team", shots="Shots",
                xG="xG", goals="G", GAX="GAX")
)
```

```{python}
teams = (
    scored.group_by(pl.col("event_team").alias("team"))
    .agg(pl.len().alias("shots"), pl.col("xg").sum().alias("xG_for"),
         (pl.col("event_type") == "GOAL").sum().alias("goals_for"))
    .with_columns((pl.col("goals_for") - pl.col("xG_for")).alias("GAX"))
    .sort("xG_for", descending=True)
)
gt_show(
    GT(teams.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Team 5v5 shot generation — season {str(latest)[:4]}-{str(latest)[4:]}")
    .fmt_number(columns=["xG_for", "GAX"], decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns="shots", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
)
```

Positive GAX marks finishing above shot quality. At the team level, xG-for
minus goals-for separates shot-generation strength from shooting luck — the
spread between the two is exactly what the embedded xG columns in
`nhl_pbp_full` exist to expose.

## Provenance & reproducibility

- **Trained on:** this repository's committed play-by-play
  (`nhl/pbp/parquet/`, seasons in the corpus table above); committed boosters
  = the 2026-04 fit; grouped 80/20 split by `game_id`, grouped 5-fold CV for
  `min_child_weight`, seed 37 (the python trainer persists the partition in
  `models/xg_model_split.json`).
- **Artifacts:** `models/xg_model_5v5.json`, `models/xg_model_st.json`
  (committed — the promotion step); python sidecars `models/xg_model_meta.json`
  (feature lists, CV + exact-holdout metrics, per-season calibration, PS
  constant) and `models/xg_model_split.json`, committed with the first
  gate-passing python retrain; every stage run appends a `models/ledger.jsonl`
  line (including failed ones). Output ships inside `nhl_pbp_full`.
- **Retrain:** `scripts/nhl_models.sh` (stages `nhl_model_01_xg_5v5` /
  `nhl_model_02_xg_st`; fingerprint-skipped when unchanged, `--force` to
  retrain); gates frozen in `models/manifest.yaml` (cv AUC floors + the ST
  per-season drift ceiling), registry row in `models/REGISTRY.md`.
- **Rebuild this document:** `scripts/render_model_docs.sh` (Quarto → GFM;
  uses this repo's `.venv` via `QUARTO_PYTHON`; `uv sync --group docs --group train`).


## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **Pre-shot context** — rush/rebound flags exist, but passing sequences and
  screens do not; public-feed models plateau here, so the honest gain is
  better rebound/rush definitions, not more trees.
- **Blocked by a gate (2026-09-01, PR #7):** *Commit the
  python meta sidecar* — the trainer now writes `models/xg_model_meta.json`
  with the exact training-time CV/holdout metrics and this document reads it
  when present, but the 2026-09-02 python retrain on this repository's parquet
  frame fell below the frozen floors (special teams cv AUC **0.7569** vs ≥ 0.81)
  and was not promoted (`models/ledger.jsonl`); the 5v5 stage of that attempt was
  not run to completion.
  Gates are never lowered; the sidecar lands with the first passing retrain.
- **Blocked by the same gate (2026-09-01, PR #7):** *Exact
  holdout reproduction* — `models/xg_model_split.json` (train/test `game_id`
  partition) is written by every python retrain and this document switches to
  the exact holdout automatically when it is committed; until then the
  evaluation is the labeled near-holdout replay.
- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #7):** *Per-season ST
  calibration drift* — monitored by the per-season table and figure above; the
  trainer records the statistic in the meta and stage `nhl_model_02_xg_st`
  gates on the observed-value-derived ceiling `max |z| ≤ _ST_DRIFT_MAX_ABS_Z`.
- **Known issue (measured 2026-09-01):** the committed 2026-04 R-trained
  boosters, scored through this repository's python feature frame,
  over-predict goals by 25–30% on every season through 2023-24 (goals/ΣxG
  0.68–0.81; |z| up to 14.8 for 5v5 and 9.2 for ST on the seed-37
  near-holdout) while 2024-25 and 2025-26 sit at 0.92–0.93, and their
  near-holdout AUC is 0.778/0.761 against the fit's 0.832/0.821. A python
  booster trained on this same frame is calibrated per season (ST max |z|
  2.008) but tops out at the same discrimination (ST cv AUC 0.7569), so the
  deficit is in the **frame**, not the booster: the R training frame and the
  python frame disagree for pre-2024 seasons. That is an R↔Python parity
  question (handed to `sdv-parity-reviewer`), not a modeling one, and it
  blocks promoting any python retrain until resolved.
